title: The Link Between Body Composition and Longevity | Spren
abstract:
## Why does body composition affect longevity?  
When body composition is assessed, we can see the percentages of lean mass, fat mass, and body fat %. Body fat can also be broken down a step further into android fat—body fat around the trunk and upper body—and gynoid fat—body fat around the hips, breasts, and thighs.  
Not only is excess fat associated with an increased mortality risk \[[10](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33437985/#:~:text=Excess%20fat%20mass%20is%20related,of%20adiposity%20such%20as%20BMI.)], but too much android fat, for example, increases metabolic syndrome risks—diabetes, high blood pressure, and obesity \[[7](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3214067/pdf/pone.0027694.pdf)]. Excessive gynoid fat also increases your risk of hypertension and may impair glucose intolerance \[[13](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18728169/#:~:text=Gynoid%20fat%20mass%20was%20positively,0.62%3B%20P%3C0.005%29.)].
## How does body composition affect longevity?  
Excessive body weight and severe obesity can cause insulin resistance, inflammation, alterations to hormonal and metabolic factors, and it even affects aging \[[1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4032609/pdf/acel0013-0391.pdf)].  
Conversely, higher percentages of lean mass—total weight of your body from non-fat sources like muscle, organs, water, connective tissue, etc.—are strongly associated with survival in older adults.  
Interestingly, increased fat mass—but not obesity—is thought to be protective in older women, whereas very low or very high-fat mass increases the risk of mortality in men \[[11](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22820447/),[3](https://agsjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/j.1532-5415.2009.02672.x)].  
Having more lean mass and muscle mass, especially as you get older, can protect against your bones becoming weaker \[[5](https://academic.oup.com/jcem/article/99/1/30/2836155)]. This reduces the risks of falling and breaking or fracturing a bone.
